correctness.rationale: The 26 vertices are the 13 points and 13 planes of F_3^3. Point vertices are independent, plane vertices form a clique, and cross adjacency is PG(2,3) incidence. With B the 13x13 incidence matrix, BB^T=3I+J. The symmetric matrix [[I,B],[B^T,B^TB]] has the graph pattern and exact rank 13, so M>=13 and therefore Z>=13. The packaged checker replays an explicit 13-vertex chronological forcing sequence, proving Z<=13. Thus Z=M=13 and real minimum rank is 13. The C++ enumerator examines all 2^26 subsets, so its coefficient census is exhaustive for this finite graph; the orbit calculation covers all minimum sets and uses a projective action independently verified to have order 5616.

value.rationale: The finding gives a complete exact zero-forcing enumerator for a natural projective-plane module-intersection graph, not just one parameter. It independently certifies minimum rank, classifies more than one million minimum forcing sets under a canonical projective symmetry, and records the point/line occupancy distribution. The ternary rank-three case is the first odd-order projective-plane instance, making it a useful exact benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
